specification.title: A nested scope completes; then the outer transaction rolls back
steps: Start the outer transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Write the marker `outer` through the framework's ordinary write API. The framework decides when it is sent: one with a unit of work may keep it pending.
Start a nested scope with the framework's nested-transaction (savepoint) API. Write the marker `inner` in it, and make sure that write was sent.
End the nested scope normally, so that its savepoint is released.
Raise an application error in the outer scope, so that the framework rolls the outer transaction back.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: A nested scope (a savepoint) that completed belongs to the outer transaction: when the outer transaction rolls back, the nested scope's writes are rolled back too.

execution.description: Declarative @Transactional on the same DataSourceTransactionManager and DriverManagerDataSource. The adapter calls a JDK proxy advised by TransactionInterceptor. It does not call the target directly. Nested work is a second call on that proxy, with PROPAGATION_NESTED or PROPAGATION_REQUIRES_NEW. The default rollback rule is RuntimeException and Error. TX-03.statement-error-rollback-not-sent is not in this mode. TX-05.explicit-serializable is not in this mode: @Transactional does not return a transaction handle.

configuration.rollbackRule: default RuntimeException and Error; TX-03.statement-error-rollback-not-sent uses rollbackFor Exception.class

execution.form: Declarative: the call goes through a JDK proxy and TransactionInterceptor. Outer PROPAGATION_REQUIRED. Inner PROPAGATION_NESTED, which DataSourceTransactionManager maps to a JDBC savepoint. Not PROPAGATION_REQUIRES_NEW.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: The caller knows that the nested scope completed, and that the outer transaction rolled back.

api_outcome.basis: the @Transactional proxy rethrew the throwable raised inside the method, so the interceptor rolled back
api_outcome.contract: Spring Framework 7.0.9 @Transactional methods run through TransactionInterceptor (org.springframework.transaction.interceptor.TransactionAspectSupport.completeTransactionAfterThrowing). The call is on a JDK proxy. The target is not invoked directly. If TransactionAttribute.rollbackOn returns true, the interceptor calls PlatformTransactionManager.rollback and rethrows the application throwable. If rollback throws TransactionSystemException, that exception replaces the application throwable and initApplicationException stores the original. If rollbackOn returns false, the interceptor calls commit. With no rollbackFor rules, RuleBasedTransactionAttribute.rollbackOn delegates to DefaultTransactionAttribute.rollbackOn, which is true for RuntimeException and Error only. The 7.0.9 reference, Rolling Back a Declarative Transaction, states: "In its default configuration, the Spring Framework's transaction infrastructure code marks a transaction for rollback only in the case of runtime, unchecked exceptions. That is, when the thrown exception is an instance or subclass of RuntimeException. (Error instances also, by default, result in a rollback)." A normal return is reported as committed. The method's own throwable leaving the proxy is reported as rolled_back. Any other throwable leaving the proxy is reported as failed. Propagation.NESTED, Spring Framework 7.0.9: "Execute within a nested transaction if a current transaction exists, behave like REQUIRED otherwise." DataSourceTransactionManager's class javadoc says nestedTransactionAllowed defaults to true and nested transactions use JDBC savepoints. Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW: "Create a new transaction, and suspend the current transaction if one exists." The statement-error case uses rollbackFor = Exception.class so a checked SQLException takes the rollback path that case describes. The default rule would commit on that checked exception. That default is not substituted for the case.
